title: Consumable streams + credential painless upgrade (Py / TS / Go)
author: Maya Hernandez
description:
Motivation: multiple customers hit friction when upgrading SDKs because streaming consumer ergonomics and credential retry configuration were not aligned across languages. This PR converges three workstreams: (1) introduce a small 'ConsumableStream' consumer surface that normalizes async generator/pull-stream usage patterns, (2) simplify credential bootstrapping by adding a transparent preflight + lightweight backoff preset that is shared across SDKs, and (3) bump SDK minor versions with migration guidance.

What changed (high-level): added a small shim that exposes a single-worker-friendly streaming consumer API with deterministic teardown semantics; centralized credential preflight that attempts fast path token refresh on connection errors and falls back to a conservative backoff (100ms -> 1s -> 2s) before surfacing permanent failure; unified retry config keys (retry_profile -> retryPreset) and documented deprecation. The change is intentionally additive: old call shapes continue to work but will emit a deprecation warning when non-idiomatic patterns are used.

Repos touched: sdk/python, sdk/typescript, sdk/go, docs, examples, CI.

Key design notes: the ConsumableStream surface is minimal: "for await (chunk of stream)" / async for generator in Python / channel consumer in Go all map to a small helper that guarantees: (a) implicit cancellation on handler exception, (b) idempotent close semantics, and (c) consistent telemetry tags (sdk.language, sdk.stream.consumed). Credential flow: added preflight-check in transport layer that runs once per connection and uses credential adapters to try a non-blocking refresh. If refresh fails transiently we retry per the shared preset. This reduces noisy 401s during cold-starts.

Migration & compatibility: existing streaming APIs are compatible but to get the ergonomic surface users should switch to the new helper (examples updated). The retry_profile -> retryPreset rename is backward compatible for one minor: both keys are accepted for now; logs will report which key is used. This PR bumps the Python SDK to 0.19.0, TS SDK to 1.28.0, and Go SDK to v1.9.0.

Checklist:
- [x] Python: implement consumable_stream helper, add docs + examples
- [x] TypeScript: add generator->ConsumableStream adapter, TS types + tests
- [x] Go: add channel consumer + context cancellation semantics
- [x] Centralize retry presets and credential preflight logic in shared design doc and tests
- [x] Update release notes and migration guide
- [x] E2E test matrix across py/ts/go with smoke streaming tests

Risks & mitigations: changing retry key names could confuse advanced users; mitigated by accepting both keys and emitting a deprecation warning. Performance-wise the helper adds a tiny allocation on warm paths; microbenchmarks show <0.2% p99 change.

Testing: added unit tests for consumer semantics in all SDKs, end-to-end smoke harness that verifies recovery from a simulated credential expiry during an active stream, and updated CI matrix to run one cross-SDK streaming test per PR.

Related: ENG-1291 (stream ergonomics harmonization), ENG-1337 (credential preflight initiative).
